name: Reverse water-gas shift for e-fuels
principle: Reverse water-gas shift (CO2 + H2 -> CO + H2O) turns CO2 into the CO needed for syngas. Topsoe's electrified RWGS reactor ran in the FrontFuel SynFuels project in Denmark from November 2024 (12 kg/h CO2) and is planned for a 2.5 ktpa synthetic fuels plant at Leuna, Germany from 2027. IEA rates CO2-to-methanol via RWGS at TRL 6 and RWGS+FT at TRL 7.

process_steps.name: Syngas to FT or methanol synthesis

performance.basis: started November 2024 with Topsoe electrified RWGS

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025 (collected in corpus/iea-reports): FrontFuel

performance.metric: CO2 conversion in reverse water-gas shift
performance.basis: Experimental RWGS: up to 65% CO2 conversion with CO energy yield up to 0.27 kg CO/kWh (about 3.7 kWh/kg CO) and under 0.1 vol% O2 in the product gas.

source.note: Jeong et al., Int. J. Hydrogen Energy (2025), read 2026-11-17

limitations: Conversion per pass and catalyst life not in sources read
